reason: Conversation 1 nailed the critical safety stop: don't touch plug or machine, isolate at the consumer unit from the dry hall, then shut off water, unplug only once dead, and get the socket checked by an electrician if wet. It then guided her safely to drain via the front filter without pulling the machine out and correctly narrowed the leak to the door seal (checking filter cap and front-vs-back), while withholding the machine from use pending repair. Conversation 2 undermined its own warning by telling her to 'turn off the washing machine immediately at the control panel' while she stood in socks on a wet floor near a live socket, prioritised an irrelevant question about water colour before power was isolated, never told her to shut off the water supply, and ended with a bare 'that is enough' plus a generic call-an-engineer with no diagnostic progress.
